newsitem.title: USA: CME live, feeder cattle end higher but gains pared.
newsitem.headline: CME live, feeder cattle end higher but gains pared.

text.p: Much of the spillover support from pork complex futures subsided late and CME live and feeder cattle futures slipped late to close with pared gains, traders said.
Live cattle closed 0.675 to 0.025 cent per lb higher with April up most at 68.150 cents. Feeder cattle ended 0.900 to 0.350 higher with May up 0.625 at 69.075 cents.

Spillover demand from the second day of limit gains in pork pits, lower grain futures and oversold conditions offset long liquidation around midday to boost live cattle for sharp gains. But further liquidation pared gains late, traders said.

Open interest remained high in the April contract. This partly offset ideas that retailers may turn their attention back to beef if pork prices start an expected rally on the Taiwan news. Demand for U.S. pork is expected to surge on the banning of pork exports from Taiwan due to an outbreak of foot and mouth disease, they said.
Packer demand for cash cattle is also seen as uncertain. They recently purchased a large amount of fed cattle and they have been cutting back on the kill rate, they added.
"They (packers) got a lot bought at $67 on Thursday" one trader said of Plains direct feedlot cattle sales.

Cargill Investor Services, Refco, R.J. O'Brien, ABN Chicogo Corp, RBH and Rosenthal Collins notably bought on the rally before selling by R.J. O'Brien, locals and spreades in April pared gains. Cargill and options traders sold June at the close. Buy stops were hit on the runup, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, commission house bought April calls on the rally but sold April 69 calls late. Commercials and locals bought June 66 calls early, pit sources added.
Feeder cattle futures found added support from the runup in live cattle which added to early strength from lower corn futures. But prices slipped late, traders said.
The firm tone to cash feeders also lent underlying support. The CME Feeder Cattle Index is expected to rise further after gains were reported at feeder auctions this week, they said.
The latest CME Feeder Cattle Index jumped $0.24 to $68.69 per cwt.
Spreading of long live cattle/short feeders limited gains early. Fund selling added to resistance in May but buying by Cargill in March spilled into other months, sources said.
Cargill and ABN Chicogo Corp spread long December live cattle/short August feeders, traders said.
Locals spread long October live/short May feeders, pit sources added.
